blocks.content: The Central Vigilance Commission shall exercise superintendence over the functioning of the Delhi Special Police Establishment in so far as it relates to the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

rows: Non-statutory body (derives powers from DSPE Act, 1946)
Investigative agency for corruption, economic offences, and major crimes
Apex advisory and supervisory body for vigilance in central administration
Functions under superintendence of CVC for corruption cases
Exercises superintendence over CBI for corruption-related cases
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
Independent agency (Submits annual performance report to President)

items: CVC's superintendence over CBI is restricted exclusively to corruption cases and does not extend to conventional crime or state-referred investigations.
CBI is a non-statutory body created by an executive resolution, whereas CVC gained statutory status via the CVC Act, 2003.
Under the CVC Act 2003, the Director of CBI is provided a guaranteed tenure of not less than two years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) exercises superintendence over the functioning of the CBI concerning offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
The Central Vigilance Commissioner heads the committee that recommends appointments for officers of the rank of SP and above in the CBI.
CBI derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946, rather than being a statutory body itself.
While CBI operates administratively under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, its corruption investigations are monitored by the CVC.
